name: Converse XMPP agent-coordination daemon
description: This project uses XMPP as a coordination layer for multiple LLM coding agents. A Converse XMPP client runs as a headless NodeJS daemon with a CLI that agents can invoke, and a /coordination skill (enabled by default via a Claude Code hook) ensures the daemon is running and has each agent join a password-restricted, members-only MUC shared with the other agents in the workspace and the human. Agents announce their tasks and statuses in the groupchat, coordinate so that when one agent's PR is merged the others become aware, rebase their own PRs and fix conflicts, and hand off newly arising sidequests to parallel Herdr tabs by asking in the MUC whether other agents are idle. Tasks can be assigned via XMPP DMs, groupchat, or Claude Code. Planned extensions include using PubSub to power a web UI with vertical swimlanes showing which agents are active, what they are working on, and for how long. The tools are harness-neutral and not locked to any particular inference provider.

description: An abstract distributed systems programming language that offers fine-grained control over resources while requiring developers to express their intent to the compiler rather than declaring machinery directly. name: Orpheum
description: A self-hosted media server for video, comparable to Plex or Jellyfin, shipping as a single Go binary deployed via Docker with a beta opening in about a month. It reaches a home server from anywhere with no port forwarding, VPN, or paywall (even behind carrier-grade NAT), supports casting to any logged-in device, and watch-together playback with synced video and voice chat that can be mixed with casting. Playback features include dialogue boost and loudness levelling per film, adaptive quality tuned for a home's upload bandwidth, and hardware transcoding with full quality in supported browsers. The library scanner explains its matches and flags guesses, and shows missing disks instead of silently vanishing titles. Data ownership is emphasized: the database is a rebuildable index, metadata corrections write back as NFO files readable by Kodi and Jellyfin, and automatic backups preserve non-derivable data (watch state, preferences, shares). Security is a primary concern: the network-facing core never opens media files or runs FFmpeg; a separate network-isolated media node handles file reads and transcodes over Unix sockets; FFmpeg is sandboxed with Landlock and seccomp; there is a small allowlisted dependency tree with pure Go and no cgo, secrets sealed at rest, optional read-only library mounting so a compromise cannot encrypt or delete media, and a cryptographically signed chain for servers and releases.
problem: Existing media servers impose paywalls, bandwidth limiting, crippled behavior, and required logins, and remote access usually demands port forwarding, a VPN, or tools like Tailscale; meanwhile the increasing pace of hacks, CVEs, and AI-assisted intrusion makes security a primary concern.

name: Bonsai
description: A voxel game engine under development for ~10 years. The world and objects in it are represented as SDF (density) fields, and the world generator and editor operate almost entirely on the GPU via a fused three-stage 'ubershader' pipeline: a user-configurable GLSL 'shaping' shader, a fused stage that convolves normals, runs a user-configurable 'decoration' function, and interprets SDF edits compiled from a graph into bytecode, and a final stage that packs occupancy, color, and normal into 32 bits. GPU results are passed back to the CPU for entity/structure spawning callbacks, then chunks are meshed with a fast binary algorithm and uploaded, retaining 16 bits per surface voxel and scaling to world sizes greater than 1B voxels cubed. The engine aims to give users both easy-to-use tools and granular control over the final output, while remaining fast.

name: Reversible incremental sorting algorithm
description: A sorting algorithm for scenarios where the cost of comparisons is high and heterogeneous, intended as a methodology for minimizing the number of pairwise human evaluations (e.g., in AI, marketing, search evaluation, and clinical trials). It tracks which pairs are solidly established, which parts of the ranking remain ambiguous, and which alternatives are still possible/impactful, deducing the fraction of the sorting that can be reused during updates — reversible incremental ranking with information-theoretic guarantees and updates that scale linearly with the number of items. It also has a machine learning application as differentiable sorting and ranking, with reported performance of 27ms and 0.18MB for sorting 8,000 items versus 1.9s and 488MB for softsort, and about 100ms and 15MB for 10^6 items, running in O(n log n) time and O(n) space like fastsoftsort while allowing linear-time ranking updates on subsequent runs.
problem: Pairwise comparisons such as human evaluations are costly and heterogeneous, and existing differentiable sorting approaches like softsort are too slow and memory-heavy to run at scale.
audience: Practitioners conducting pairwise human evaluations in AI, marketing, search evaluation, and clinical trials

It also has a machine learning application as differentiable sorting and ranking, with reported performance of 27ms and 0.18MB for sorting 8,000 items versus 1.9s and 488MB for softsort, and about 100ms and 15MB for 10^6 items, running in O(n log n) time and O(n) space like fastsoftsort while allowing linear-time ranking updates on subsequent runs. Pairwise comparisons such as human evaluations are costly and heterogeneous, and existing differentiable sorting approaches like softsort are too slow and memory-heavy to run at scale. Practitioners conducting pairwise human evaluations in AI, marketing, search evaluation, and clinical trials Xmd5a

description: An open-source library that extends the torchvision API to 3D object detection tasks. description: This app is an open source coding agent named Loa designed to run against self-hosted LLM environments such as Ollama, targeting non-cloud-sized models (e.g. a 27b model). name: SpecPilot
description: SpecPilot is a spec-driven development layer that sits in front of AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and others. It deliberately doesn't generate code itself; instead it scaffolds a .specs/ folder and hands spec writing off to whichever agent is already in use, so specs become the artifact the agent is held to rather than a prompt retyped every session. It began as an open-source TypeScript CLI and was later given a guided chat front door of 27 questions that runs fully offline in the browser, outputting the .specs/ tree plus an IDE onboarding prompt. A recently shipped MCP server (published to the official MCP registry and Smithery) lets the agent run the questionnaire itself, and planned brownfield support would point the tool at an existing repo and backfill specs from the code. The tool is free, open source, and has no login; the author sees spec enforcement — checking diffs against specs and failing loudly — as where the lasting value lies.

name: Fabulae Orbilii
description: A Latin language audiobook site presenting both volumes of A.D. Godley's "The Fables of Orbilius", entertaining intermediate Latin stories written at the turn of the 20th century for use in British schools. Audio is delivered in restored classical Latin pronunciation with spoken nuances such as vowel nasalization, elision, and prodelision. A wav2vec2 model generates forced-alignment data so readers can follow along with the text as it is read aloud, and each word is enriched with pedagogical details including lemma, citation forms/principal parts, morphological segmentation and analysis, inflectional class with declension/conjugation tables, contextual lexical (L&S) sense, Classical Latin IPA pronunciation, UD-style syntactic function and relations, predicate valency, and concise English definitions. The documents are entirely XML, rendered in-browser via XSLT so the underlying XML structure is visible, with per-sentence provenance records showing the language model and parameters used for each enrichment task. The site UI is bilingual, viewable in Latin or English.
